metadata.title: Goldman's New AI Office Adds Just 1% to Its Engineering Army

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS), the global investment-banking and asset-management firm, opened a new engineering office in Bellevue, Washington, built around artificial intelligence and cloud modernization. The stock hovered near flat Tuesday morning, edging roughly 0.03% lower to $1,038.74.
The office will house more than 125 employees, a modest addition beside Goldman's army of over 12,000 engineersroughly one-quarter of its worldwide workforce. Bellevue's real appeal is geography: Goldman can recruit from the deep technology pool surrounding Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN) while pushing AI deeper into banking operations. The headcount is small. The potential reach is not.
Goldman's second-quarter results delivered record net revenue of $20.34 billion, net earnings of $6.63 billion and a 23.5% annualized return on equity. The shares also trade 25.85% above the $825.37 GF Value estimate, signaling that investors already expect plenty from the business. Bellevue must now produce measurable gains in productivity, risk control or revenuenot merely another polished AI announcement.
